correctness.rationale: PASS applies to the replacement RESULT.md, not to the original positive-octant assertion. In the original coordinates, a=b=1 and (x,y,z)=(1,1,2) give a strictly positive H=1 point other than E_+ that maps to E_-=(1,−1,0) in one step rather than oscillating. The repaired text explicitly lists (1/b,1/√(ab),1+1/b), always positive, and E_+ only when b>1. This is exactly the intersection of the eight sign choices with the original positive octant. Rechecking the whole theorem: 1−z_{n+1}=x_n gives y_{n+3}=ab y_{n+2}y_n²; zero data force eventual zero, and other data give L_{n+3}=L_{n+2}+2L_n. The left projection w·U_0=log H and w·v=3r²−2r yield the leading r-mode, exact H power law, and strict-region limits because 1<s<r. Varying |x| locally on H=1 proves the common boundary. In the nonzero complementary mode the expanding rotation produces infinitely many strictly positive and strictly negative sinusoidal excursions, for both rational and irrational angles; its full log-vector norm diverges, precluding recurrence. Vanishing initial log vector gives exactly the eight sign cases and arrival at an E_± within two steps. Poincaré recurrence on a countable basis gives the three-Dirac probability census, and the normalized monomial log chart gives the three repelling eigenvalues at E_±. The derivative at E_0 is nilpotent.
